question.text: India deposited its MLI instrument of ratification with the OECD on 25 June 2019 and notified provisions effective 1 October 2019. In the context of treaty benefits available to non-resident investors in a Cat III AIF, MLI principally introduces:

answer.text: A Principal Purpose Test (PPT) and / or Limitation of Benefits (LOB) clauses
A blanket denial of treaty benefits to all non-residents
A mandatory 20% TDS on all treaty countries
A replacement of Section 115UB with Section 115UA

explanation.text: The Logic: The OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI), arising from BEPS Action 15 and operative through Article 7, implements treaty anti-abuse rules — principally the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) and, optionally, a Limitation of Benefits (LOB) clause. Under the PPT, treaty benefits can be denied where obtaining the benefit was one of the principal purposes of an arrangement, unless granting the benefit is in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant treaty provision. The Trap: Option B is an over-statement — MLI does not deny all treaty benefits to non-residents. Option C is incorrect — TDS rates are set under the Income-tax Act, not the MLI. Option D conflates Section 115UB (Category I/II AIF pass-through) with Section 115UA (business trusts such as REITs/InvITs). Note: The specific framing of PPT and LOB as MLI provisions is not explicitly stated in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages. Those pages support MLI as a treaty-related BEPS instrument aimed at preventing inappropriate treaty benefits and treaty-shopping, and reference LOB only in the GAAR clarification context. The PPT/LOB framing above reflects the OECD MLI text and general international-tax practice.
